1. The present ref

erence is u/s 30 & 31 of Land Acquisition Act, 1984 whereby a sum of Rs.1,31,239.23/- was deposited with court with request to adjudicate the inter se dispute between various claimants detailed in the reference.
2. As per the reference received, the dispute between the different claimants is dispute of compensation.

3. After the reference was received by the Ld. Predecessor of this Court on 15.10.2021,
after repeated non-appearance of the interested parties (arrayed as R-1 to R-7), the reference was adjourned sine die with liberty given to the interested parties to revive the same as and when they so desire.

4. Eventually, the present reference was revived at the instance of IP no. 4 and IP no.
5 (hereinafter referred to as 'R-4 and R-5' respectively) vide order dated 24.05.2025.
5.
The said respondents have preferred their claim before this court.

As per the claim filed by R-4 and R-5, they purchased the acquired land from R-1 to R-3 by way of two separate registered sale deeds both dated 12.03.1987.
6.
Thus, R-4 and R-5 are before this court seeking apportionment of their share in terms of the said sale deeds in their favour.

7. I may note that as per the sale deeds placed on record, out of the total land acquired under the award in question (measuring 4 bighas 3 biswas), R-4 and R-5 had purchased 1/3rd share each in the said land.
The remaining 1/3rd share was purchased by R-6 (who remained ex-parte before this court) vide a separate sale deed also dated 12.03.1987.

8. It is pertinent to note that in the written reply filed by R-7 (who filed its reply as IP no. 7), was admitted by R-7 that R-4 to R-6 had purchased the land under acquisition by virtue of registered sale deeds dated 12.03.1987.
But, as per reply of R-7, after the said sale deeds, R-4 to R-6 had executed GPA, Agreement to Sell and receipt etc in favour of R-7 on 19.12.1987.

Some consideration is also stated to have been paid by the said R-7 in favour of R-4 to R-6.
9.
I may note that as per the reference made to this court, R-1 to R-3 are the recorded owners of the land under acquisition.
They never entered appearance before this court despite opportunity.

Again,
R-6 also did not enter appearance before this court.

10. Thus, only R-4 and R-5 have preferred a claim before this court on the ground that based on their respective sale deeds dated 12.03.1987, they are entitled to 1/3rd share of the amount deposited in court.

3 11.
R-7 had resisted the said claim by filing its reply and contending that R-7 had purchased the said land from R-4 to R-6 by way of GPA, agreement to sell dated 19.12.1987.
12. Thus, the only issue before this court is as to which person is entitled to receive the compensation deposited in court and the apportionment thereof?

13. Before proceeding further, I may note that R-5/Anil Sharma had expired before the present reference could be decided and his interest is represented by his wife Manju Sharma and his minor son Krishna Sharma.
14. R-4/Chandrakala had proved on record the sale deed dated 12.03.1987 Ex.PW1/1.
The concerned record clerk from the office of Sub Registrar was summoned by the said respondent as IPW-1.
This witness proved that R-4 holds a registered sale deed in her name qua 1/3rd share in the land acquired by the award referred above.
The said sale deed was executed by R-1 to R-3 (the recorded owners of the land as per revenue records).
15. Similarly, R-5/Anil Sharma (through his legal representatives) had proved on record the sale deed dated 12.03.1987 Ex.PW1/2.
The concerned record clerk from the office of Sub Registrar was summoned by the said respondent as IPW-1.
This witness proved that R-5 holds a registered sale deed in his name qua 1/3rd share in the land acquired by the award referred above.
The said sale deed was executed by R-1 to R-3 (the recorded owners of the land as per revenue records).

16. As per record, R-5/Anil Sharma died sometime in 2021 and his wife/Manju Sharma stepped in the witness box as IP3/A to assert that she is the legal heir of R-5 entitled to receive compensation awarded to R-5 under the award in question.
17. Thus, as per the said documents, R-4 and R-5 hold registered sale deed in their favour qua 1/3rd share each in the land acquired by the award referred above.

18. Even though, R-7 has resisted the petition by filing a written reply, no evidence was led by R-7 to prove their claim that R-4 to R-6 had further sold their right, title or interest in the land in question to R-7.

Even otherwise, the documents relied upon by R-7 are in the nature of GPA, agreement to sell etc which by themselves cannot create any right, title or interest in the land in favour of R-7 (see Suraj Lamp & Industries (P) Ltd. vs State Of Haryana & Anr. AIR 2012 Supreme Court 206).
19.

sentences.text: Thus, as per record, R-4 and R-5 (through his LRs) are held to be entitled to receive 1/3rd share in the total compensation deposited in court.
Since R-5 had expired, his LRs i.e. Manju Sharma and his minor son Krishan Sharma are entitled to receive the share falling in hands of R-5.
Krishan Sharma is stated to be minor and is represented before this court through his mother Manju Sharma.
She shall be entitled to receive the compensation on her behalf as well as on behalf of her son Krishan Sharma.
It is ordered accordingly.

21. The present reference stands answered qua the 2/3rd sum lying deposited in the court.
